key_claims: Al-Qa'ida's Afghanistan camps played a central role in planning the 11 September attacks and selecting and training the cadres.
Selection into al-Qa'ida occurred only in Afghanistan after observing candidates in training.
Al-Faruq camp near Kandahar was preferred for second-wave hijackers because of proximity to Bin Ladin.
Without a safehaven al-Qa'ida will struggle to train and vet recruits and will lose leverage over allied groups.
Al-Qa'ida has shifted to small-scale training in madrasas, refugee camps and Pakistani border regions.
